name: Making big models smaller and faster
gist: Papers on compressing models and running them efficiently using low-rank updates, mixing specialized experts, or removing unnecessary parameters.
explain: Modern machine learning models can have billions of parameters — numbers that the model uses to make predictions. A model that big can process information and pick up subtle patterns, but it requires massive computing power to run. If you want a model to work on a phone, in a car, or on a tiny device in a factory, you need to shrink it. The key question is how to find and remove the parameters that do not contribute much to predictions, so the model stays smart without getting bloated — because every parameter you remove saves memory and computing time.

The hard part is that the large model's power comes from its size. Every parameter contributes something to the prediction. If you simply delete parameters, the model gets worse. But often, parameters are redundant — many of them are doing almost the same thing, or their contribution is tiny. You need to find which parameters matter and which ones are passengers. Even when you identify the important ones, you have to retrain the model so the remaining parameters adapt and compensate for the ones that are gone.

Researchers use several strategies. Some compress the model by representing it in a more efficient way — for example, using low-rank factorization, which represents large matrices as products of smaller matrices, the way you might factor a big number into smaller primes. Some use sparse updates, where each specialized mini-model (called an expert) handles one kind of input, so only some of the model's parameters activate for each prediction, which saves computation. Some round numbers to fewer bits (the way images on a computer use fewer colors than in real life yet still look right), making the model lighter to store and faster to run because fewer numbers mean less data to process. Some combine these approaches together, which makes the savings multiply — so the resulting model is small, runs fast, and works well because each technique removes a different kind of waste.

papers.title: AQER: A Scalable and Efficient Data Loader for Digital Quantum Computers
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and gate efficiency across synthetic, image, language, and quantum many-body datasets up to 50 qubits.

papers.title: Composable Sparse Subnetworks via Maximum-Entropy Principle
papers.contribution: Trained subnetworks achieve high accuracy on target classes with minimal leakage, and combined modules often recover generalist performance with interpretable functional structure.

papers.title: DisTaC: Conditioning Task Vectors via Distillation for Robust Model Merging
papers.contribution: Enables state-of-the-art merging techniques to successfully integrate models that would otherwise fail, achieving significant performance gains in realistic settings.

papers.title: Ensemble Prediction of Task Affinity for Efficient Multi-Task Learning
papers.contribution: Improves MTL gain prediction and enables more effective task grouping, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines across benchmark datasets in diverse application domains.

papers.title: Knowledge Distillation as Decontamination? Revisiting the “Data Laundering” Concern
papers.contribution: Demonstrates laundering is exception rather than rule with smaller effects than direct contamination and correlates with large train-test gaps, suggesting distillation effectively mitigates test-data leakage.

papers.title: Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models through Residual Learning
papers.contribution: Residual learning for distillation enables students to improve representations beyond teacher knowledge, with expert-fusion via self-attention for MoE teachers and cross-model attention for cross-tokenizer settings.

papers.title: MicroMix: Efficient Mixed-Precision Quantization with Microscaling Formats for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves near-FP16 performance at 5-bit average precision and 2.29-3.38x acceleration on Llama and Qwen models.

papers.title: xRFM: Accurate, scalable, and interpretable feature learning models for tabular data
papers.contribution: Achieves best performance across 100 regression datasets and competitive results on 200 classification datasets, outperforming recent tabular foundation models and GBDTs.

papers.title: AMiD: Knowledge Distillation for LLMs with $\alpha$-mixture Assistant Distribution
papers.contribution: Offers superior performance and training stability compared to previous assistant distribution approaches through broader and theoretically grounded framework.

papers.title: AlphaSAGE: Structure-Aware Alpha Mining via GFlowNets for Robust Exploration
papers.contribution: AlphaSAGE outperforms existing baselines in mining more diverse, novel, and highly predictive alpha portfolios, establishing a new paradigm for automated alpha mining.

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Criterion for Efficient Data Synthesis
papers.contribution: Results not specified.

papers.title: Boosted Trees on a Diet: Compact Models for Resource-Constrained Devices
papers.contribution: Achieves 4-16x compression ratio compared to LightGBM models while maintaining same performance, enabling autonomous edge devices.

papers.title: CAR-LoRA: Training Compression-Aware and Robust LoRA Adapters for Evolving LLMs
papers.contribution: Yields unified adapter robust to diverse compression artifacts and parameter shifts from model evolution.

papers.title: CauchyNet: Compact and Data-Efficient Learning using Holomorphic Activation Functions
papers.contribution: CauchyNet achieves lower error on near-singular and gap-filling benchmarks with substantially fewer trainable parameters in target regimes.

papers.title: CogMoE: Signal-Quality–Guided Multimodal MoE for Cognitive Load Prediction
papers.contribution: CogMoE outperforms baselines with consistent improvements across diverse signal qualities; introduces CORTEX Loss balancing reconstruction and expert utilization.

papers.title: Combination-of-Experts with Knowledge Sharing for Cross-Task Vehicle Routing Problems
papers.contribution: CoEKS achieves 12% improvement over SOTA on unseen constraint combinations and 25% on new constraints while maintaining in-distribution performance.

papers.title: Efficient and Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

papers.title: SALAAD: Sparse And Low-Rank Adaptation via ADMM for Large Language Model Inference
papers.contribution: Single training run yields continuous spectrum of model capacities enabling elastic deployment without retraining.

papers.contribution: Addresses NTC limitations theoretically and practically, establishes discrete binary structures as viable path toward optimal rate-distortion bounds.

papers.title: Synchronizing Probabilities in Model-Driven Lossless Compression
